title: Real files vs. live kernel views

steps.title: Some of / is on disk, some is the kernel talking
steps.body:
The root filesystem on the SD card holds programs and configuration. `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev` are not on any disk: the kernel generates them as you read.

The values shown are real ones from this board.

steps.title: The ext4 root holds what you build and ship
steps.body:
Everything on this panel is an ordinary file on partition 1 of the SD card: `/bin`, `/usr`, `/etc`, `/root`, `/home` and `/var/log`.

The next steps pick out the directories that matter most to the boot process.

steps.title: /boot is what U-Boot loads
steps.body:
It holds `Image.gz` and the 47 DTBs. U-Boot reads the kernel and your board's device tree from here, so replacing a file here changes what boots.

It is also where `uEnv.txt` lives.

steps.title: Modules and firmware are looked up at runtime
steps.body:
The `.ko` drivers and `modules.alias` live under `/lib/modules/6.18.20-custom`. Firmware that drivers request, such as SDMA and audio, comes from `/lib/firmware/imx`.

A kernel without a matching modules directory cannot load its drivers.

steps.title: /sbin/init is PID 1
steps.body:
The kernel ends its boot by running this program, which is BusyBox or systemd. It reads `/etc` (`inittab`, `fstab`, hostname, network, ssh) and starts everything else.

If it is missing, the kernel panics at the end of boot.

steps.title: /proc exposes processes and kernel state
steps.body:
`cat /proc/cmdline` shows `console=ttymxc1,115200 root=/dev/mmcblk1p1 …`, `/proc/cpuinfo` shows 4 × Cortex-A53, and `/proc/meminfo` gives MemTotal and CmaTotal.

`ps` and `free` just read these files.

steps.title: /sys exposes the device model
steps.body:
Each device the kernel found has a directory here: the RTC at `/sys/bus/i2c/devices/3-0068`, temperature at `thermal_zone0/temp` (57000 means 57 °C), `eth1/carrier` (1 means cable in).

`/sys/firmware/devicetree/base` is the DTB U-Boot passed.

steps.title: /dev holds device nodes created when drivers probe
steps.body:
`/dev/mmcblk1p1` is the SD card's root partition, `/dev/ttymxc1` is the serial console, and `/dev/rtc0` and `/dev/i2c-3` appear once their drivers probe.

That is why a missing driver means a missing node.

steps.title: Takeaway: reading a file asks the kernel a question
steps.body:
init mounts these three at boot. Reading a file there asks the kernel a question; writing one, such as `echo` to `/sys/class/leds/…`, changes hardware state.

That is how most commands in the board-use chapter work.
